runs.u: Can you recommend a project-management tool?
runs.reply:
Because the "best" project management tool depends entirely on your team size, workflow, and budget, I have categorized the top recommendations based on what they do best. 

Here is a breakdown of the top project management tools on the market today:

---

### 1. Monday.com (Best All-Rounder)
Monday.com is highly visual, extremely customizable, and great for teams of all sizes. It uses a spreadsheet-like interface that can be easily transformed into Kanban boards, timelines (Gantt charts), or calendars.
*   **Best for:** General business teams, marketing agencies, and operations.
*   **Pros:** Highly intuitive, beautiful UI, excellent automation features (e.g., "When status changes to Done, notify Manager"), and great templates.
*   **Cons:** Pricing can get expensive quickly as you add team members.
*   **Free Plan:** Very limited (up to 2 users).

### 2. Asana (Best for Collaboration & Task Tracking)
Asana is designed to help teams coordinate who is doing what, by when. It is less about spreadsheets and more about clear task lists, timelines, and workloads.
*   **Best for:** Cross-functional teams, creative projects, and medium-to-large companies.
*   **Pros:** Very easy to delegate tasks, great timeline (Gantt) views, and clean user experience. Excellent for seeing team workloads.
*   **Cons:** Can feel overwhelming if not set up correctly; no built-in time tracking (requires integrations).
*   **Free Plan:** Very generous (up to 10 users with basic features).

### 3. Trello (Best for Simplicity & Kanban)
Trello popularized the "Kanban board" (moving cards from "To Do" to "Doing" to "Done"). It is incredibly simple and requires almost zero training to use.
*   **Best for:** Individuals, freelancers, and small teams with straightforward workflows.
*   **Pros:** Extremely easy to use, fast setup, and highly visual.
*   **Cons:** Not suited for complex projects, deep reporting, or managing large budgets/resources.
*   **Free Plan:** Great free plan (unlimited users, up to 10 boards).

### 4. ClickUp (Best "All-in-One" Tool)
ClickUp’s slogan is "One app to replace them all." It combines tasks, docs, goals, calendars, whiteboards, and even inbox features into a single platform.
*   **Best for:** Power users and startups who want one tool to do everything.
*   **Pros:** Highly customizable, feature-rich, and offers great value for the price.
*   **Cons:** Can be overwhelming for beginners (high learning curve); the mobile app can be slow.
*   **Free Plan:** Excellent free tier with lots of features.

### 5. Jira (Best for Software & Tech Teams)
Jira (by Atlassian) is the industry standard for software development. It is built specifically for Agile, Scrum, and Kanban methodologies.
*   **Best for:** Software developers, product managers, and IT teams.
*   **Pros:** Unmatched for bug tracking, sprint planning, and release management. Integrates perfectly with GitHub, Bitbucket, etc.
*   **Cons:** Notoriously complex to set up; interface is clunky and not friendly for non-technical teams (like marketing or HR).
*   **Free Plan:** Free for up to 10 users.

### 6. Notion (Best for Knowledge Management + PM)
Notion is a "connected workspace" where you can write docs, build wikis, and manage projects using databases.
*   **Best for:** Creators, startups, and remote teams who need to document *everything* while managing tasks.
*   **Pros:** Ultimate flexibility; you can build exactly what you need. Great AI features.
*   **Cons:** You have to build your own system from scratch (or use templates), which takes time.
*   **Free Plan:** Very generous for personal use; cheap team plans.

---

### How to Choose:
*   If you want **simplicity and speed**: Go with **Trello**.
*   If you want a **beautiful, highly automated system**: Go with **Monday.com**.
*   If you are a **software/tech team**: Go with **Jira**.
*   If you want **maximum features for the lowest price**: Go with **ClickUp**.
*   If you want a tool that does **documentation and project tracking**: Go with **Notion**. 

If you can share a bit about your **team size, industry, and what you are trying to manage**, I can give you a more specific recommendation!

To give you the best recommendation, it helps to know which country you are in. However, assuming you are in the **United States**, the market is divided into two main types of carriers: **The Big Three** (major networks with the best perks/speeds) and **MVNOs** (budget carriers that run on the major networks but cost much less).

Here is a breakdown of the best mobile carriers for 2024 based on different needs:

---

### 1. Best Budget Carriers (MVNOs)
*These carriers lease coverage from the major networks, offering the exact same signal strength for a fraction of the price.*

*   **Mint Mobile (Best Value Overall)**
    *   **Network:** T-Mobile
    *   **Cost:** Starts at $15/month (if you prepay for 3, 6, or 12 months).
    *   **Best for:** People who want high-speed data at the lowest possible price and don’t mind paying upfront for several months of service.
*   **Visible by Verizon (Best Cheap Unlimited)**
    *   **Network:** Verizon
    *   **Cost:** $25/month (basic) or $45/month (Visible+, which includes premium data and smartwatch service).
    *   **Best for:** Single users who want truly unlimited data, mobile hotspot, and Verizon's reliable coverage without a high monthly bill.
*   **US Mobile (Most Flexible)**
    *   **Network:** You can choose between T-Mobile (Light Speed), Verizon (Warp), or AT&T (Dark Star).
    *   **Cost:** Plans start at around $15 to $44/month.
    *   **Best for:** People who want to choose their preferred network and customize their data plans. They also allow you to switch networks easily.

---

### 2. Best Major Carriers (The Big Three)
*Best for families, heavy data users, those who want phone upgrades/financing, or people who want perks like streaming services.*

*   **T-Mobile (Best Performance & Perks)**
    *   **Pros:** Fastest 5G speeds nationwide, great perks (Netflix, Apple TV+ on premium plans), and taxes/fees are included in the advertised price. Excellent international roaming.
    *   **Cons:** Coverage in very rural areas can still lag slightly behind Verizon.
*   **Verizon (Best Overall Coverage)**
    *   **Pros:** The most reliable network coverage, especially in rural areas. They offer customizable "MyPlan" options where you can add perks (like Disney+ or Apple One) for $10/month.
    *   **Cons:** The most expensive option; taxes and fees are extra.
*   **AT&T (Best Consistency & Phone Deals)**
    *   **Pros:** Very reliable network. They frequently offer the best phone upgrade deals, giving the same discounts to both new and existing customers.
    *   **Cons:** Plans are expensive, and their customer service can be frustrating.

---

### 3. Best for International Travel
*   **Google Fi Wireless**
    *   **Network:** T-Mobile
    *   **Best for:** Frequent international travelers. Their "Unlimited Plus" plan ($65/line) includes seamless data, calling, and texting in over 200 destinations at no extra cost.

---

### How to Choose:
To help narrow this down, consider these three questions:
1.  **What is your budget?** (Under $30/month? Or is unlimited premium data worth $70+?)
2.  **How many lines do you need?** (Major carriers offer massive discounts for 3–4 lines; budget carriers are usually better for 1–2 lines).
3.  **Which network has the best coverage in your area?** (Ask neighbors or look at coverage maps to see if T-Mobile, Verizon, or AT&T works best in your home/office). 

*If you can share your approximate location (or country), budget, and how many lines you need, I can give you a specific recommendation!*

**My Choice:** **T-Mobile (specifically the "Go5G Plus" plan)**

*   **Why I’d pick it:** If you have 3 or more lines, or if you want the fastest possible speeds and free phone upgrades, T-Mobile is currently beating Verizon and AT&T.
*   **The Network:** T-Mobile currently has the **fastest and most widespread 5G network** in the US.

*   If you want to save money and only need **1 or 2 lines**, go with **Visible**.
*   If you have a **family (3+ lines)** and want the best speeds, perks, and phone deals, go with **T-Mobile**.
